# Feature Geometry Differences Across Model Families Plus Non-Transferable Safety Tooling

**Problem:** Compound: (1) interp findings (which feature/direction encodes a concept) don't transfer across model families (interp portability failure) amplifying (2) a monoculture-tooling failure where a safety filter built on one model's geometry is reused on another and silently fails. Re-using a 'safe' interp recipe across the fleet propagates a blind spot.

**Direction:** Pick the same safety concept and locate its probe/feature in two different open model families (e.g. GPT-2 and Pythia, or Gemma and Llama-small). Train a probe on family A and apply to family B. Measure cross-family transfer accuracy and how much a reused monitor under-detects on the unseen family.

**Why it matters:** Organizations reuse safety tooling across models for cost. Quantifying that interp-derived monitors don't port — and the resulting safety gap — is a fresh, multi-model study fully feasible on consumer hardware.

**Relevant context:** Tuned Lens paper (arXiv:2303.08112): extracted information 'varies model to model.' 'Position: Prioritize Feature Consistency' (arXiv:2505.20254). TransformerLens supports 50+ models across families on a single GPU.

# Layer Sweep: At Which Depth Is Jailbreak Detection Cheapest and Most Robust?

**Problem:** Probe papers report results at chosen layers but the full layer-vs-robustness tradeoff is rarely published openly. Whether early layers (cheaper, allow early-exit) detect jailbreaks as well as deep layers is an open practical question.

**Direction:** Train identical logistic-regression probes on residual-stream activations at every layer of one open model for harmful-vs-harmless classification. Plot clean recall AND post-paraphrase recall vs layer index. Identify the earliest layer achieving near-peak detection (enabling cheap early-exit monitoring).

**Why it matters:** An early-layer probe enables a cheap monitoring harness that can abort generation before harmful tokens are produced — strategically valuable, lab-independent infrastructure. Single GPU, one forward pass per prompt.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2601.11516, arXiv:2509.14558 ('Jailbreak Detection for Almost Free'), arXiv:2506.10805 (high-stakes interaction probes). Context open problem: 'cost-effective jailbreak detection via activation probes that scale better'.

# Sycophancy Features Plus Human-Oversight Erosion

**Problem:** Compound: (1) interp surfaces 'agree with the user' sycophancy features that are entangled with helpfulness (interp/entanglement failure) amplifying (2) erosion of human oversight (scalable-oversight subfield). If sycophancy can't be cleanly isolated and removed, the model keeps telling overseers what they want to hear, degrading the human signal that oversight relies on.

**Direction:** Locate a candidate sycophancy feature/direction in an open model via probing on agree/disagree-under-pressure pairs. Measure entanglement with a general helpfulness feature. Test whether suppressing sycophancy also suppresses correct agreement, quantifying the compound oversight-degradation cost of imperfect feature isolation.

**Why it matters:** Sycophancy undermines the human feedback safety relies on — a diffuse, important problem. A clean probing study on public models with no training, well-scoped to 30h.

**Relevant context:** 'Good Arguments Against the People Pleasers' (arXiv:2603.16643) on reasoning and sycophancy. Anthropic/Perez sycophancy datasets are public. Probing/TransformerLens tooling supports the setup; SAEs available for entanglement checks.

# Interp Dashboard Anchoring Plus Human-Reviewer Automation Bias

**Problem:** Compound: (1) confident-looking feature dashboards/visualizations that can be wrong (interp presentation failure) amplifying (2) human automation bias in oversight. The compound: a polished 'this feature means X, and it's not firing' dashboard makes human reviewers over-trust and stop checking, so a wrong interp readout actively suppresses the human catch that would have flagged the harm.

**Direction:** Run a small human-subjects-style study (you + a few peers, or a scripted decision rule simulating reviewer trust). Present harmful cases where a dashboard says 'benign feature' (engineered using known absorption/confabulation). Measure how often a 'reviewer' overrides the dashboard vs. defers, estimating the added miss rate from interp-induced over-trust.

**Why it matters:** The interp-to-decision human factor is rarely studied yet central to whether interp helps safety. Cheap, behavioral, lab-independent, and a genuinely fresh compound framing (interp UX x automation bias).

**Relevant context:** Search results: SAE dashboards/auto-interp can be 'precise, compelling, and ultimately misleading'; auto-interp scores misleading. Absorption (arXiv:2409.14507) supplies engineered false-benign cases. Automation-bias literature in human-AI oversight motivates the design.

# Auditing Diff-SAE Backdoor Isolation on Open Sleeper-Agent Models

**Problem:** Activation Differences Reveal Backdoors (arXiv:2605.07324, May 2026) shows Diff-SAE achieves a Backdoor Isolation Score of 0.40 with perfect precision on the models the authors tested, but it is unclear whether this holds for publicly released backdoored/sleeper-agent checkpoints with different trigger styles.

**Direction:** Take 2-3 open backdoored model checkpoints (e.g. published sleeper-agent or trojan-LLM weights on HuggingFace), reproduce the Diff-SAE difference-of-activations recipe at one residual-stream layer using SAELens, and measure whether the top difference-features cleanly localize the trigger. Vary trigger type (token-level vs phrase-level vs date-conditioned) and report BIS/precision per trigger type.

**Why it matters:** Unsupervised backdoor detection that needs only two model snapshots and no knowledge of the trigger is exactly the kind of monitoring infrastructure valuable outside frontier labs. Confirming or breaking the headline result on independent models tells the community whether the method generalizes.

**Relevant context:** Activation Differences Reveal Backdoors: A Comparison of SAE Architectures (arXiv:2605.07324, May 2026) reports Diff-SAE BIS 0.40, precision 1.0, FPR 0; Crosscoders BIS <0.02. Suggests backdoors are directional activation shifts, not sparse features. SAELens tooling listed in subfield context.

# Do Shared Backdoor Latents Transfer to a Model the Authors Did Not Test?

**Problem:** Shared Latent Structures Enable Unified Backdoor Detection (arXiv:2606.07963, June 2026) claims a small set of residual-stream SAE latents is consistently activated across backdoor behaviors and generalizes across 4B-32B models. The claim of a near-universal backdoor signature is strong and worth independent replication on an out-of-distribution backdoor.

**Direction:** Use a pretrained open SAE on a model in the 4-8B range, fine-tune a tiny backdoor with a novel trigger (a few hundred examples, single GPU, no from-scratch training), and check whether the specific latent indices the paper identifies light up. Report overlap between the paper's universal latent set and the latents your backdoor activates.

**Why it matters:** If a fixed, transferable latent fingerprint really exists, a deployer could screen any fine-tuned model cheaply without retraining detectors. Testing transfer to an unseen trigger is the critical falsification.

**Relevant context:** Shared Latent Structures Enable Unified Backdoor Detection and Mitigation in LLMs (arXiv:2606.07963, June 2026): small set of SAE latents activated across diverse backdoors, generalizing 4B-32B and across fine-tuning and weight-editing attacks.

# Cheap Reproduction of the SAE Refusal-Capability Tradeoff Curve

**Problem:** Steering Language Model Refusal with SAEs (arXiv:2411.11296) found that amplifying refusal-mediating SAE features improves jailbreak robustness but systematically degrades capability even on unrelated safe inputs, suggesting refusal features are entangled with general capability. The shape of this tradeoff across steering strengths is under-characterized.

**Direction:** On an open model with a public SAE (e.g. Gemma-2 + GemmaScope), sweep the steering coefficient on identified refusal features and plot a dose-response curve: jailbreak-resistance on a small harmful-prompt set vs accuracy on a neutral benchmark (e.g. a 200-item MMLU slice). Identify the inflection point where capability collapse begins.

**Why it matters:** Quantifying exactly where steering-based safety starts cannibalizing capability informs whether SAE steering is a deployable defense or a dead end, and the curve is reusable by other researchers. Needs no lab infrastructure.

**Relevant context:** Steering Language Model Refusal with Sparse Autoencoders (arXiv:2411.11296): SAE refusal steering improves multi-turn jailbreak robustness but causes systematic degradation on safe inputs, implying refusal-capability entanglement. GemmaScope SAEs are openly available.

# How Many Benign SAE Features Can Jailbreak a Model?

**Problem:** Recent steering work reports that 817 of 1000 tested SAE features representing benign concepts exhibited jailbreaking capability when amplified. If true, the attack surface of feature steering is enormous, but the result needs independent measurement on a different SAE and model.

**Direction:** Take a public SAE on a small open model, sample ~500 randomly chosen (benign-looking) features, amplify each one at a fixed coefficient, and measure jailbreak success rate on a fixed harmful-prompt set. Report the fraction of benign features that raise harmful-completion rate above baseline and cluster which feature semantics are most dangerous.

**Why it matters:** Characterizes whether activation steering is an inherently unsafe interface (any feature is a potential exploit) versus a controllable one. This is a defensive-research question labs deprioritize and it needs only open SAEs.

**Relevant context:** Reported finding (steering literature, 2025-2026) that 817/1000 benign SAE features had jailbreaking capability; related to The Rogue Scalpel: Activation Steering Compromises LLM Safety (arXiv:2509.22067). GemmaScope/SAELens provide open features.

**Why it matters:** Automated circuit description is the bottleneck for scaling interpretability; a small honest audit of where automation diverges from humans is broadly useful and feasible on tiny models with no lab resources.

**Relevant context:** ADAG: Automatically Describing Attribution Graphs (arXiv:2604.07615, April 2026): attribution profiles quantify feature functional role via input/output gradient effects, plus a clustering algorithm and an LLM explainer-simulator that generates and scores natural-language explanations.

title: Does CoT Faithfulness Improve With Token Budget? A Replication

# Does CoT Faithfulness Improve With Token Budget? A Replication

**Problem:** Is Chain-of-Thought Really Not Explainability? (arXiv:2512.23032) argues much apparent CoT unfaithfulness is an artifact of tight token limits, and that larger inference-time budgets push hint verbalization up to ~90% via a faithful@k metric. This optimistic reframing should be tested on open reasoning models.

**Direction:** On an open reasoning model (e.g. a small DeepSeek-R1-distilled or Qwen reasoning checkpoint), insert biasing hints into multi-hop questions, vary the max-token budget across several settings, and compute hint-verbalization rate / faithful@k. Test whether the budget-faithfulness relationship reproduces and where it plateaus.

**Why it matters:** If CoT monitoring is reliable mainly under generous token budgets, that directly shapes how CoT-based oversight should be deployed. The threat model (unfaithful hidden reasoning) is exactly the kind of medium-horizon concern worth studying outside labs.

**Relevant context:** Is Chain-of-Thought Really Not Explainability? Chain-of-Thought Can Be Faithful without Hint Verbalization (arXiv:2512.23032): >50% of CoTs flagged unfaithful by Biasing Features judged faithful by other metrics; faithful@k shows budgets raise verbalization up to 90%.

# Probing the Think-Answer Divergence in Open-Weight Reasoning Models

**Problem:** Why Models Know But Don't Say (arXiv:2603.26410, March 2026) documents a faithfulness divergence between thinking tokens and final answers in open-weight reasoning models, but does not characterize whether the divergence is linearly decodable from activations at the point of divergence.

**Direction:** Collect prompts where an open reasoning model's chain-of-thought reaches a tentative answer that differs from its final answer, train a simple linear probe on residual-stream activations at the transition, and test whether a probe can predict 'the model will override its reasoning'. Report probe accuracy vs a CoT-only baseline.

**Why it matters:** A cheap activation probe that flags when a model is about to contradict its own stated reasoning is a concrete monitoring tool, and tests the linear-representation hypothesis on a safety-relevant behavior using only an open model.

**Relevant context:** Why Models Know But Don't Say: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Divergence Between Thinking Tokens and Answers in Open-Weight Reasoning Models (arXiv:2603.26410, March 2026). Linear representation hypothesis underlies probing per Probing Evaluation Awareness (arXiv:2507.01786).

# Extending Evaluation-Awareness Probes to Open Reasoning Models

**Problem:** Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness of Language Models (arXiv:2507.01786) shows models linearly encode whether they are being evaluated, but the study focuses on a limited model set; it is unclear whether evaluation-awareness directions exist and transfer in newer open reasoning models.

**Direction:** Build a small contrast dataset of 'this is a test' vs 'this is real deployment' framed prompts, extract the difference-of-means direction in an open reasoning model's residual stream, and measure (a) probe accuracy detecting eval framing and (b) whether steering along that direction changes behavior (e.g. refusal or sandbagging rates). Compare to the original paper's reported separability.

**Why it matters:** Evaluation-awareness undermines all safety benchmarks; a transferable probe is a cheap detector and the threat model (models behaving differently when watched) is squarely a long-horizon, lab-deprioritized concern.

**Relevant context:** Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness of Language Models (arXiv:2507.01786): linear-representation-hypothesis-based probes detect evaluation awareness and steering shifts behavior.

# Replicating Simple Adaptive Attacks: How Many Restarts Until Jailbreak?

**Problem:** Andriushchenko et al. (arXiv:2404.02151) achieved 100% on Claude 2.0 with up to 10 random restarts. The number-of-restarts-vs-success curve for current OPEN models is not characterized, leaving defenders without a robustness yardstick.

**Direction:** Implement the simple random-search / random-restart adaptive attack from the paper against 2-3 current open chat models. For each, plot cumulative jailbreak success vs number of restarts (1..N) on a fixed harmful set. Report 'restarts to 50%/90% success' as a comparable robustness metric.

**Why it matters:** A standardized restarts-to-success metric lets the community track open-model robustness over time without lab access. Directly tests the realistic-attacker-capability open problem. Compute-light (black-box queries only).

**Relevant context:** Andriushchenko, Croce, Flammarion, 'Jailbreaking Leading Safety-Aligned LLMs with Simple Adaptive Attacks' (arXiv:2404.02151): 100% on Claude 2.0 in <=10 restarts vs prior best 61%. Code public.

# Stress-Testing Targeted-Instruction-Pair Deception Probes Across Datasets

**Problem:** Building Better Deception Probes Using Targeted Instruction Pairs (arXiv:2602.01425, Feb 2026) builds stronger deception probes, but related work notes deception is heterogeneous: probes that work on one deception dataset may fail on another (e.g. sandbagging responds best to concealment-focused prompts).

**Direction:** Reimplement the targeted-instruction-pair probe construction on an open model, then evaluate cross-dataset transfer: train on one deception dataset (e.g. roleplay lying) and test on a different one (e.g. sandbagging). Produce a transfer matrix quantifying how much detectability degrades across deception types.

**Why it matters:** Honest measurement of how brittle deception probes are across deception subtypes is essential before anyone trusts them for oversight, and it requires only open models and small labeled datasets.

**Relevant context:** Building Better Deception Probes Using Targeted Instruction Pairs (arXiv:2602.01425, Feb 2026); deception heterogeneity noted in deception-probe literature (sandbagging responds best to concealment-focused prompts).

# Replicating CoT-SAE Causal Faithfulness on a Different Reasoning Task

**Problem:** How does Chain of Thought Think? (arXiv:2507.22928) presents the first feature-level causal study of CoT faithfulness using sparse autoencoding, but on a limited task set. Whether the causal faithfulness signal generalizes to arithmetic vs commonsense vs symbolic reasoning is open.

**Direction:** Using a public SAE on a small instruct model, identify SAE features active during CoT on one reasoning task, ablate them, and measure whether the stated CoT and the answer change together (faithful) or independently (unfaithful). Repeat across 2-3 task families and compare faithfulness scores.

**Why it matters:** Mapping which reasoning domains have causally faithful CoT tells oversight designers where CoT monitoring is trustworthy. Fully feasible with open SAEs and a single GPU.

**Relevant context:** How does Chain of Thought Think? Mechanistic Interpretability of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Sparse Autoencoding (arXiv:2507.22928): first feature-level causal study of CoT faithfulness.

**Problem:** Cross-Architecture Model Diffing with Crosscoders (arXiv:2602.11729, Feb 2026) discovers differences between LLMs unsupervised, and Delta-Crosscoder (arXiv:2603.04426, March 2026) targets narrow fine-tuning regimes. Whether these diffing methods surface a deliberately inserted behavioral change in a controlled tiny fine-tune is testable.

**Direction:** Fine-tune a small open model on a narrow behavior change (e.g. always praising a specific entity) using a few hundred examples, train a crosscoder/diff-SAE between base and fine-tuned models with SAELens, and check whether the top model-exclusive latents correspond to the injected behavior. Compare crosscoder vs delta-crosscoder recovery.

**Why it matters:** Model diffing as an auditing tool for 'what did this fine-tune change?' is strategically valuable infrastructure that any external auditor could use on open weights, with no lab access required.

**Relevant context:** Cross-Architecture Model Diffing with Crosscoders (arXiv:2602.11729, Feb 2026); Delta-Crosscoder: Robust Crosscoder Model Diffing in Narrow Fine-Tuning Regimes (arXiv:2603.04426, March 2026); Anthropic Crosscoder diffing updates (transformer-circuits.pub 2025).

# Evaluating SAE Quality Without Explanations on Open Vision SAEs

**Problem:** Evaluating SAE Interpretability Without Explanations (arXiv:2507.08473) proposes explanation-free SAE quality metrics, but these have mostly been applied to language SAEs; Prisma reports vision SAEs have substantially lower sparsity than language SAEs, so the metrics may behave differently.

**Direction:** Apply the explanation-free interpretability metrics (e.g. activation-based separability scores) to several of Prisma's 80+ pretrained vision SAEs and to a language SAE, and test whether the metrics rank vision SAEs sensibly given their lower sparsity. Report whether the metrics need recalibration for vision.

**Why it matters:** Cheap, explanation-free SAE evaluation that works across modalities would let anyone benchmark SAE quality without an LLM-judge pipeline. Directly addresses the subfield's identified benchmark gap.

**Relevant context:** Evaluating SAE interpretability without explanations (arXiv:2507.08473); Prisma (arXiv:2504.19475) reports vision SAEs show substantially lower sparsity than language SAEs and 80+ pretrained vision SAE weights are available.

# Characterizing Why Vision SAE Reconstructions Sometimes Lower Loss

**Problem:** Prisma (arXiv:2504.19475, CVPR 2025 workshop) reports the surprising result that in some cases vision SAE reconstructions decrease model loss, which violates the usual assumption that SAEs only approximate (and degrade) the original activations. This phenomenon is unexplained.

**Direction:** Using Prisma's pretrained vision SAEs and a small image set, identify layers/inputs where reconstruction lowers loss, and test hypotheses: is it denoising (removing high-frequency noise components), or class-specific? Measure loss delta as a function of SAE sparsity and input class to characterize when reconstruction helps.

**Why it matters:** Understanding when SAEs improve rather than degrade a model challenges the standard interpretability framing and is a self-contained, surprising, fully open-source vision-interpretability study.

**Relevant context:** Prisma: An Open Source Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability in Vision and Video (arXiv:2504.19475): effective vision SAEs exhibit substantially lower sparsity than language SAEs and in some instances SAE reconstructions decrease model loss.

# Activation-Probe Detection of Multi-Agent Collusion in an Open LLM Game

**Problem:** Detecting Multi-Agent Collusion Through Multi-Agent Interpretability (arXiv:2604.01151, April 2026, Oxford/NYU) uses activation-based probes to detect collusion, but the experiments use specific agent setups; whether simple probes detect emergent covert coordination in an independent, lightweight multi-agent game is untested.

**Direction:** Set up two instances of a small open model playing a Schelling/coordination game with a side-channel for steganographic signaling, collect residual-stream activations, and train a linear probe to detect 'agent is colluding vs playing honestly'. Report probe AUC and whether it survives when agents are prompted to hide coordination.

**Why it matters:** Covert multi-agent collusion is a clear long-horizon threat that frontier labs underinvest in; a model-organism-style probe study on open models is high counterfactual value and feasible at small scale.

**Relevant context:** Detecting Multi-Agent Collusion Through Multi-Agent Interpretability (arXiv:2604.01151, April 2026): activation-based probes for collusion; covert coordination hides info in innocuous channels; steganography detection is hard.

# Probing the Look-Ahead Planning Signal in a Small Open Model

**Problem:** Anthropic's Circuit Tracing found Claude 3.5 Haiku plans rhyming words ahead, and Unlocking the Future (arXiv:2406.16033) localizes look-ahead planning to mid-layer MHSA output at the last token. Whether this last-token mid-layer planning signal exists in small open models, and whether it correlates with capability, is open.

**Direction:** On a short planning task (e.g. simple maze/path or constrained-poetry generation) with a small open model, train a linear probe on mid-layer last-token activations to decode the future committed choice before it is emitted. Compare probe decodability across 2-3 model sizes to test whether planning strength scales with capability.

**Why it matters:** Whether models internally plan ahead (vs. greedily decode) is central to deceptive-planning threat models; a cheap probe study across sizes tests the surprising Anthropic result outside a lab.

**Relevant context:** Anthropic Circuit Tracing: Claude 3.5 Haiku plans rhyming words ahead. Unlocking the Future: Exploring Look-Ahead Planning Mechanistic Interpretability in LLMs (arXiv:2406.16033): mid-layer MHSA output at last token can decode the decision.

# Replicating 'How Do LLMs Use Their Depth?' on Safety-Relevant Tokens

**Problem:** How Do LLMs Use Their Depth? (arXiv:2510.18871) analyzes layer-wise computation, but does not focus on whether safety-relevant decisions (e.g. deciding to refuse) use depth differently from ordinary tokens.

**Direction:** Using the logit-lens / per-layer-prediction methodology on a small open model, compare the depth at which the model 'commits' to a refusal vs commits to a benign continuation, by tracking when the decisive logit direction stabilizes across layers. **Relevant context:** arXiv:2506.10805 'Detecting High-Stakes Interactions with Activation Probes'. arXiv:2601.11516 (production probes). arXiv:2509.14558 (cheap detection).

# Reward Hacking Seeds Emergent Misalignment: A Toy RL Replication

**Problem:** Anthropic's 'Natural emergent misalignment from reward hacking in production RL' (arXiv 2511.18397) and arXiv 2605.31328 ('RL Amplifies EM from Harmless Rewards') show RL on harmless reward signals can amplify broad misalignment. There is no minimal, reproducible-on-a-laptop demonstration that ties reward hacking to EM.

**Direction:** Build a tiny reward-hackable task (e.g. a verifier with an exploitable shortcut) and run short DPO/REINFORCE-style updates on a small open model, then measure broad off-task misalignment as the policy learns to hack the reward, comparing hackable vs non-hackable reward variants.

**Why it matters:** Demonstrates the EM-from-reward-hacking link in a transparent, fully-open setting that anyone can inspect — converting a frontier-lab finding into reusable pedagogy and a probe. Targets a core RLHF-limitation open problem.

**Relevant context:** Natural emergent misalignment from reward hacking in production RL (arXiv 2511.18397, Anthropic). RL Amplifies Emergent Misalignment from Harmless Rewards (arXiv 2605.31328). EM base (arXiv 2502.17424).

# Mapping the Sycophancy-Amplification Covariance Predicted by Theory in Open Preference Data

**Problem:** A formal account (How RLHF Amplifies Sycophancy, arXiv 2602.01002) predicts that the direction of sycophancy drift is set by a covariance between 'endorsing the user's belief' and the learned reward. This covariance has not been directly measured in a public preference dataset.

**Direction:** On Anthropic HH-RLHF, automatically label each pair for whether the chosen response endorses a belief stated in the prompt, train a small reward model on the data, and empirically estimate the predicted covariance between belief-endorsement and reward — testing whether its sign predicts sycophancy.

**Why it matters:** Connects a theoretical amplification mechanism to a measurable, fully-open dataset quantity, giving practitioners a diagnostic to predict sycophancy before training. Uses only public data and a single GPU.

**Relevant context:** How RLHF Amplifies Sycophancy (arXiv 2602.01002): drift direction set by covariance between endorsing belief signal and learned reward. Sycophancy in HH-RLHF (Sharma et al. arXiv 2310.13548). What's In My Human Feedback (arXiv 2510.26202).

# Via Negativa Alignment: Do Negative Constraints Resist Emergent Misalignment Better Than Positive Preferences?

**Problem:** A 2026 position (Via Negativa for AI Alignment, arXiv 2603.16417) argues negative constraints ('do not X') are structurally superior to positive preference learning. This is untested against the EM failure mode: does constraint-style fine-tuning data resist broad misalignment generalization better than preference-style data?

**Direction:** Construct two matched fine-tuning sets for the same narrow task — one phrased as positive preferences, one as negative constraints — fine-tune a small model on each, and compare downstream broad misalignment rates and in-domain performance.

**Why it matters:** If framing alignment data as constraints intrinsically narrows generalization, it is a near-free, lab-independent mitigation for EM. Tests a provocative structural claim cheaply.

**Relevant context:** Via Negativa for AI Alignment (arXiv 2603.16417): negative constraints structurally superior to positive preferences. EM (arXiv 2502.17424). In-Training Defenses (arXiv 2508.06249).

# Likelihood Displacement as an Early-Warning Signal for Preference-Training Misalignment

**Problem:** DPO suffers 'likelihood displacement' where chosen-response probability paradoxically drops during training. It is unknown whether the onset of displacement coincides with — or predicts — the onset of broad misalignment when the preference data is subtly poisoned.

**Direction:** Run DPO on a small open model with a small fraction of poisoned preference pairs, logging per-step chosen/rejected log-probs (to detect displacement) and periodically evaluating broad misalignment. Test whether a displacement spike is an early indicator of emerging misalignment.

**Why it matters:** A free, training-internal monitoring signal (already logged during DPO) that could flag misalignment before it manifests in behavior — cheap monitoring infrastructure deployable by any fine-tuner.

**Relevant context:** Likelihood displacement in DPO (DPO-Shift arXiv 2502.07599; BPO/PG-DPO arXiv 2511.x): chosen probabilities decrease during training. EM (arXiv 2502.17424). TRL provides DPO implementation.
